empire: The Empire is the mightiest human nation in the Old World, sustained by the Elector Count system, the Cult of Sigmar, the Colleges of Magic, and the Imperial Gunnery and Engineering Guilds. Its vast territories span the basins of the Reik, Talabec, and Stir rivers, extending north to the stormy coast of Nordland, south to the Black Mountains, west to the Grey Mountains, and east to the imposing World's Edge Mountains. Altdorf, Middenheim, Talabheim, and Nuln form the structural quadrilateral of the Empire, encircled by wheat fields, managed forestries, vineyards, gristmills, stone keeps, and paved Imperial roads that bind human settlements into a unified realm. Yet beneath this surface cohesion lies perpetual tension: the fierce Cult of Ulric in the north questions Sigmarite supremacy, rival Elector Counts zealously guard their provincial privileges, and hidden Chaos cults gnaw at the moral fiber of the cities. Under the freshly crowned Emperor Karl Franz, the Empire must deploy its versatile State Troops, thunderous Great Cannons, and lethal Hellblaster Volley Guns alongside legendary knightly orders and battle wizards to repel ceaseless incursions while holding a fractious realm together.
vlandia: The Kingdom of Bretonnia sprawls across the fertile lowlands, meandering river valleys, and verdant foothills of the western Old World—a realm where devout worship of the Lady of the Lake, the strictures of Chivalry, and an unyielding feudal hierarchy are woven into an indivisible sacred order. The ducal citadels of Couronne, Bordeleaux, Aquitaine, and the blighted ruins of Mousillon form the kingdom's historical pillars, surrounded by sprawling manorial estates, vineyards, pastures, and stone chapels maintained by the labor of impoverished peasant levies. Through sacred vows of fealty, the fiefdom system, and the overarching religious authority of the Grail Dames and Damsels, Bretonnia fields the most devastating cavalry charges in the known world. Knights of the Realm, Questing Knights seeking the sacred chalice, and peerless Grail Knights who have drunk of the Lady's power form an iron-shod thunderbolt. Under King Louen Leoncoeur, the Golden King, Bretonnia strives to embody chivalric purity even as peasant unrest, dark curses in Mousillon, and looming northern darkness test the kingdom's resilience.
khuzait: The Vampire Counts hold dread dominion over Sylvania on the Empire's eastern frontier—a cursed, fog-shrouded wasteland where eternal storm clouds block the sun and the very earth is steeped in Dhar, the dark wind of magic. Castle Drakenhof, Waldenhof, Essen, and Tempelhof constitute the black heart of this blighted domain, ringed by tangled, haunted forests, desecrated graveyards, withered crops, and cowed villages. Through dark bloodlines, unholy pacts, and the primordial necromantic legacies of Nagash, the dead rule over the living with absolute authority. Sylvanian mortals live lives of grim subservience, locking their shutters at twilight as corpse carts creak through muddy streets. Led by cunning schemers like Count Mannfred von Carstein, the nocturnal lords command legions of skeletal warriors, shambling zombies, fell bats, and ghostly crypt horrors. They do not seek to merely raid their mortal neighbors, but to harvest human souls and claim the Imperial throne in Altdorf as an immortal dynasty.
battania: The Wood Elves—who style themselves the Asrai—are the reclusive guardians of the magical forest of Athel Loren, possessing the oldest, most insular, and deadliest archery culture in the Old World. Athel Loren is neither a kingdom of brick and stone nor a realm of roads and treaties; it is a living, breathing, semi-sentient ecosystem bound to the fate of the Asrai through ancient covenants. The King's Glade, the seasonal courts of Amethyst and Amber, the Oak of Ages, and countless hidden hollows form a subterranean network of roots that span across dimensions. Deepwood Scouts, Waywatchers, Glade Guard, and towering Treemen move through the canopy like phantoms, their deadly bodkin arrows and nature magics slaying trespassers before they even realize they are being hunted. Under the immortal King in the Woods, Orion, and the Fay Queen Ariel, the Asrai maintain armed isolation, unleashing the terrifying Wild Hunt whenever their sacred borders are desecrated.
chaos_culture: The Warriors of Chaos represent the apocalyptic hammer of the northern wastes—an unstoppable scourge dedicated to the total annihilation of the mortal order. They do not constitute a nation or a dynasty, but the unbridled will of the Chaos Gods manifest upon the physical world. From the icy fjords of Norsca, the frozen wastes of the Troll Country, and the abyssal ruins of the collapsed Polar Star Gates, dark champions gather to prove their devotion to Khorne, Nurgle, Tzeentch, and Slaanesh. Clad in suits of ensorcelled hellforged plate armor and wielding daemon-imbued axes, Chaos Warriors and Chosen march alongside marauder hordes, monstrous Chaos Spawn, and towering Dragon Ogres. Driven by the apocalyptic prophecies of the Everchosen, they view southern realms as decadent corruptions marked for divine cleansing, descending in screaming iron tides to drown civilization in blood and madness.
aserai: The Greenskins—encompassing brutal Orcs and cunning Goblins—are the most pervasive, unpredictable, and indestructible catastrophe in the Old World. They do not merely invade civilization; they are embedded into the very soil, reproducing via fungal spores that flourish in the most hostile environments. From the cracked desert gorges of the Badlands to the crags of the Grey Mountains, and from abandoned dwarf galleries in the World's Edge Mountains to the deepest, darkest primeval forests of the Empire, Greenskin tribes lurk everywhere. Orc Boyz, hulking Black Orcs, frenzied Savage Orcs, and treacherous Night Goblins worship the brawling twin gods Gork and Mork. When a sufficiently terrifying Warboss gathers enough victories, an uncontrollable, roaring green cataclysm known as the Waaagh! erupts, sweeping over forts, karaks, and cities in a riotous tidal wave of cleavers, squigs, and raw brute savagery.
sturgia: The Dwarfs—who call themselves the Dawi—are an ancient, tragic race of mountain folk clinging to survival in their subterranean fortress-cities carved into the granite spines of the World's Edge Mountains and Grey Mountains. Karaz-a-Karak, the Everpeak, serves as the seat of the High King and the sacred heart of Karaz Ankor, yet the vast subterranean network of Underway roads that once connected legendary holds like Karak Eight Peaks, Karak Varr, and Karak Kadrin lies mostly collapsed or overrun by night goblins and skaven. Dwarfen culture is defined by runic mastery, unmatched gromril metallurgy, and an unyielding commitment to the Dammaz Kron—the Great Book of Grudges. Heavily armored Ironbreakers and Hammerers form an unbreakable shield wall, supported by organ guns, cannons, and steam-driven Gyrocopters. Led by High King Thorgrim Grudgebearer, the Dwarfs wage a grim, unforgiving war of reclamation to avenge their fallen ancestors and reclaim the lost glory of the mountain holds.
averland: Averland occupies the sunlit, rolling plains and fertile alluvial basins of the southeastern Empire, bounded by the Black Mountains and the River Reik. Renowned across the Old World for its peerless horse-breeding, vast cattle ranches, and rich vineyards, Averland is the primary bulwark guarding Black Fire Pass—the treacherous defile through which greenskin Waaaghs! and southern invaders routinely surge toward the Imperial heartland. The provincial capital of Averheim, built atop ancient Sigmarite battle sites, is governed by the notoriously mercurial yet militarily brilliant Elector Count Marius Leitdorf. The province fields elite regiments of Bergjaeger mountain scouts and lavishly equipped knightly lances. Balancing the eccentricities of its court with relentless frontier vigilance, Averland stands as an unbreakable shield barring the terrors of the south from the civilized north.
stirland: Stirland is one of the oldest, poorest, and most superstitious provinces in the Empire. Straddling the River Stir and bordering the cursed wastes of Sylvania, its rugged landscape of rolling moors, dense pine thickets, and misty bogs breeds a hardy, taciturn populace. From the provincial capital of Wurtbad, nestled against steep valley cliffs, Elector Count Alberich Haupt-Anderssen oversees a realm perpetually on edge. Stirland's archers and halberdiers are renowned for their grim resilience, trained from childhood to watch the shadows for ghouls, zombies, and the midnight nobility. Plagued by poverty and border disputes with Averland and the Moot, Stirland endures through unbending faith in Sigmar and Morr, knowing that if its vigil falters, the restless dead of Sylvania will consume the Empire from within.
wissenland: Wissenland lies in the southwestern cradle of the Empire, framed by the jagged peaks of the Grey Mountains and Black Mountains. While the ancient castle of Pfeildorf serves as its titular seat, the true economic and military nucleus of the realm is Nuln—the jewel of the Reik, the largest manufacturing metropolis in the Old World, and the official arsenal of the Empire. Ruled by the glamorous Countess Emmanuelle von Liebwitz, Nuln is home to the world-famous Imperial Gunnery School and the College of Engineering. Day and night, blast furnaces roar as master foundries cast Great Cannons, Mortars, and experimental Hellblaster Volley Guns. Wissenland's state troops are among the best-equipped in the realm, relying on disciplined pike-and-shot formations and devastating barrages to secure mountain choke points against greenskins and beastmen.
talabecland: Talabecland spans the vast geographic heart of the Empire, stretching over a thousand kilometers along the sacred River Talabec. Its capital, Talabheim, is one of the defensive wonders of the known world—built entirely inside the colossal, cratered depression of an ancient meteor strike known as the Taalbaston, whose towering granite walls form an impregnable natural ring fortress. Ruled by Elector Count Helmut Feuerbach, the people of Talabecland revere Taal, God of Beasts and Wild Places, alongside his consort Rhya. The province is blanketed by the ancient canopy of the Great Forest, a wilderness teeming with beastmen warherds, forest goblins, and renegade cults. Talabecland's State Troops, clad in red and yellow liveries, are seasoned woodsmen who patrol the waterways and highways, anchoring the Empire's central trade and defense.
reikland: Reikland is the beating heart, crown jewel, and political nexus of the Empire. Nestled in the fertile basin between the Grey Mountains and the confluence of the Reik and Talabec rivers, its capital is Altdorf—the imperial seat, spiritual center of the Cult of Sigmar, and home to the Eight Colleges of Magic. As the ancestral hereditary domain of Emperor Karl Franz, Reikland is the wealthiest and most populous province in the realm. Its commercial waterways bustle with barge traffic connecting Marienburg, Nuln, and the Border Princes. Reikland's armies, clad in immaculate white liveries, include the elite Reiksguard Knights, the Emperor's personal Carroburg Greatswords, and state-of-the-art artillery regiments. From the majestic Imperial Palace, Karl Franz must wield both silver-tongued diplomacy and the hammer of Sigmar to hold a fractured realm together.
middenland: Middenland is the towering bastion of the northern Empire, a windswept province defined by primeval woodlands, fierce winter gales, and the ancient faith of Ulric, God of Wolves, Winter, and War. Its legendary capital, Middenheim—the City of the White Wolf—is perched atop the Fauschlag, a sheer five-hundred-foot plateau of solid granite accessible only by colossal viaducts, making it virtually impregnable. Under the grim, iron-willed rule of Graf Boris Todbringer, Middenland wages a perpetual war against the beastmen and greenskins infesting the dark depths of the surrounding Drakwald Forest. Middenland's warriors, including the ferocious Knights of the White Wolf wielding two-handed warhammers and the elite Teutogen Guard, scorn excessive ornament, fighting with primal fury to defend humanity's northern gateway against the encroaching shadow of Chaos.
ostermark: Ostermark, formally known as the League of Ostermark, is the Empire's rugged northeastern frontier march, stretching between the River Talabec, the frozen kingdom of Kislev, and the crags of the World's Edge Mountains. Its capital, Bechafen, stands as a heavily fortified redoubt against raiding warbands descending from the northern steppes. Ostermark's history is steeped in tragedy and sacrifice: here lies the catastrophic crater of Mordheim, the City of the Damned, destroyed by a warpstone comet centuries ago. Chancellor Wolfram Hertwig governs a resilient populace of hunters, horse-archers, and hardened border infantry clad in purple and yellow. Accustomed to frequent skirmishes with Marauders, Greenskins, and Night Goblins, Ostermark functions as an indispensable early-warning outpost shielding the Imperial interior from eastern devastation.
hochland: Hochland is one of the smallest and most heavily forested provinces of the Empire, nestled between Middenland, Ostland, and Talabecland in the shadow of the Middle Mountains. Densely blanketed by the ancient Drakwald and Forest of Shadows, Hochland is a province of rugged foresters, charcoal burners, and expert hunters. Its fortified capital, Hergig, guards the vital trade crossings linking the northern provinces. Under Elector Count Aldebrand Ludenhof—an avid falconer and master shot—Hochland has achieved continental fame through its invention of the Hochland Longrifle, a superbly accurate sniper weapon capable of eliminating enemy commanders from extreme distances. Hochland's green-and-red liveried Jaegers and huntsmen form the eyes and ears of the northern Empire, ambushing enemy warbands before they can breach the forest canopy.
nordland: Nordland is the Empire's sole coastal province, stretching along the stormy, fog-bound shores of the Sea of Claws. Governed from the fortified seat of Salzenmund by Baron Theoderic Gausser, Nordland is squeezed between two towering ancient forests: the Forest of Shadows to the east and the enigmatic Laurelorn Forest to the west, home to the independent Eonir elves. Nordland's culture is steeped in maritime lore and endless vigilance against brutal Norscan longship raids. Its people are skilled sailors, whalers, and coastguards who patrol chilly fjords and rocky shingle beaches. Blue-and-yellow-uniformed Nordland state troops and mariners guard coastal towns while walking a diplomatic tightrope with the reclusive elven Queen of Laurelorn, ensuring humanity retains its naval gateway to the northern seas.
ostland: Ostland sits at the exposed northeastern shoulder of the Empire, forming the front-line shield wall against the nightmares of the Chaos Wastes and Troll Country. Almost the entirety of the province is enveloped by the sinister Forest of Shadows—a perilous wilderness infested with blood-drinking briars, feral beastmen, and lurking monsters. From the battered fortified capital of Wolfenburg, Elector Count Valmir von Raukov rules with soldierly grit, spending more time in the saddle with his bow and runefang than in council halls. Ostland's warriors, clad in black and white, are celebrated for their stubborn tenacity and lethal bowmanship. Having repelled countless invasions from the northern wastes, the people of Ostland know that if their shield line breaks, the horrors of the north will sweep unopposed into the Imperial heartland.
wasteland: The Wasteland—historically known as Western March before seceding from the Empire—is an autonomous merchant republic centered on the mouth of the River Reik. Its crowning jewel is Marienburg, the largest, wealthiest, and most cosmopolitan seaport in the Old World, built upon the misty delta islands and ancient elven ruins of Sith Rionnasc. Governed by the oligarchic Directorate and Stadsraad under Burgomeister Luitpold van Reimerswaal, Marienburg bought its independence from Emperor Dieter IV with a legendary chest of gold. The city's canals bustle with elven merchant clippers, dwarfen ironclads, Tilean galleons, and Kislevite traders. Protected by heavily funded mercenary armies, merchant guild militias, and an armada of warships, Marienburg fiercely guards its commercial hegemony, ensuring no foreign crown dictates terms at the gateway to the western sea.
moot: The Mootland is the smallest, youngest, and most eccentric Electoral province of the Empire—the official homeland of the Old World Halflings. Nestled in the lush alluvial basin where the Blue Reach joins the River Aver, the Moot was carved out of southern Stirland in 1010 IC by Emperor Ludwig the Fat, who granted the Halflings an Imperial Charter and an Electoral vote in gratitude for their culinary and agricultural genius. Governed by Elder Hisme Stoutheart from the idyllic riverside market town of Saurapfel, the Moot is a tranquil paradise of burrows, orchards, and rolling wheat fields. While disdaining heavy armor and formal militarism, Halfling fieldwardens and gamekeepers possess peerless stealth and dead-eye slingshot marksmanship, fiercely defending their beloved pantry and sovereign hearth against any who dare disturb their peace.
couronne: Couronne is the sacred heartland and royal crown of the Kingdom of Bretonnia, ruled directly by King Louen Leoncoeur in his dual capacity as Duke of Couronne and High King of the realm. Perched upon a majestic ocean promontory above the River Sannez, Couronne's towering palace is built upon the ancient, sun-bleached foundations of an elven citadel. The vast rolling plains of Couronne are the breeding grounds for the finest purebred warhorses in the Old World—the celebrated Couronne destriers, whose speed and iron constitution carry the realm's chivalric charges. As the premier center of worship for the Lady of the Lake, the Tournament of Couronne draws Questing and Grail Knights from every corner of the kingdom. Louen, the Lionhearted, leads from the front mounted upon his mighty hippogryph Beaquis, embodying the golden age of Bretonnian chivalry against the looming storm of northern devastation.
anguille: L'Anguille is a wealthy maritime dukedom hugging the northern coast of Bretonnia, nestled between Lyonesse to the west and Couronne to the east. Its capital port city of L'Anguille is built atop the monumental ruins of Tor Alessi, an ancient High Elven fortress-haven. Dominating the harbor is the breathtaking Dragon Lighthouse—a soaring, thousand-foot tower of seamless white elven stone whose magical beam guides ships through the treacherous tides of the Great Ocean. Ruled by Duke Taubert, L'Anguille boasts the largest and most cosmopolitan naval fleet in Bretonnia. While knightly traditions remain strong, the dukedom's character is heavily shaped by sea captains, merchants, and naval skirmishers. L'Anguille wages a continuous maritime war against Norscan reavers, ensuring the sea lanes of the west remain open to trade.
lyonesse: Lyonesse spans the windswept northwestern shores of Bretonnia, famous throughout the Old World for two defining features: its labyrinth of island castles and its tangled aristocratic rivalries. Divided by geography and politics into North and South Lyonesse, the northern territory is the ancestral heartland of Thierulf, companion of Gilles le Breton, while the south borders the cursed, plague-ridden marshes of Mousillon. Governed by Duke Adalhard, Lyonesse is a rugged land of sunken coasts, sea cliffs, and tidal islands where fortified castles rise like granite sentinels from crashing waves. Hardened by centuries of repelling coastal pirates, sea monsters, and the creeping rot of Mousillon's undead, the knights of Lyonesse are fiercely independent pragmatists whose heavy lances guard the western marches of the realm.
artois: Artois is unique among the Bretonnian dukedoms: almost its entire territory is smothered beneath the primeval canopy of the mysterious and dangerous Forest of Arden, with only a narrow strip of arable farmland along its western border. Ruled from the fortified woodland castle of Larret by Duke Chilfroy, Artois is a realm locked in perpetual wilderness warfare. Beastmen brayherds, mutated predators, and forest goblins haunt the shadows beneath the ancient trees. Artois's knights spend their lives not in gleaming tournaments, but in silent ambushes, hunting monsters with heavy boar spears alongside peasant woodsmen armed with yew longbows. Living in a world of gloom, mist, and sudden death, the people of Artois are Bretonnia's indispensable woodland sentinels.
gisoreux: Gisoreux is situated in the transitional zone between the chalky heights of the Pale Sisters and the dark borders of the Forest of Arden, possessing the most diverse geography and culture in Bretonnia. Divided into four distinct regions—the fertile southern lowlands, the northern plains, the Arden forest march, and the jagged Grismerie mountain valley—Gisoreux is governed by the wise and diplomatic Duke Hagen. The capital city of Gisoreux straddles the River Grismerie, serving as the commercial gateway connecting northern Bretonnian ports to the Grey Mountain passes leading into the Empire. Gisoreux's knights are seasoned mountain and forest fighters, adept at coordinating heavy cavalry with hill archers to crush greenskins and beastmen descending from the highlands.
parravon: Parravon is perched high along the rugged eastern frontier of Bretonnia, clinging to the jagged granite precipices of the Grey Mountains. It guards the Grey Lady Pass, one of the three vital overland trade routes linking Bretonnia to the Empire. Parravon is world-renowned for its singular military marvel: it is the ancestral home of the Pegasus Knights. Amidst the dizzying cliffs and sheer canyon walls, wild Pegasi nest in aeries inaccessible to mortal men. Guided by Duke Cassyon—the youngest and boldest of Bretonnia's dukes—noble youths scale sheer precipices to tame these winged steeds. Swooping from cloud-shrouded peaks, Parravon's Pegasus Knights strike enemy flanks with lance-point precision, policing mountain passes and crushing greenskin ambushes from the sky.
montfort: Montfort is an austere alpine dukedom pressed entirely against the jagged spine of the Grey Mountains. It holds the perilous responsibility of guarding Axe Bite Pass—the primary overland trade artery connecting Bretonnia with Reikland in the Empire. With virtually no arable land, Montfort relies on sheep herding, iron and silver mining, and highway tariffs to survive. From Castle Montfort, carved directly into the sheer living rock of the mountain gorge, Duke Folcard oversees a garrison of grim mountain fighters. Montfort's knights frequently fight dismounted as heavy men-at-arms in tight gorges, supported by hardy mountain yeomen and skilled crossbowmen. Enduring brutal blizzards and endless greenskin raids, Montfort stands as an unyielding granite barrier at the gateway between empires.
bastonne: Bastonne is the spiritual, historical, and heroic heart of Bretonnia. It was here that Gilles le Breton slew the colossal red dragon Smearghus, met the Lady of the Lake in the sacred groves, and drank from the Holy Grail to become the first Grail Knight and King. Governed by the legendary Duke Bohemond the Beastslayer, Bastonne is a land of rolling chalk hills, deep forests, and sacred shrines. Its knights are famed for their reckless courage and dragon-slaying tradition, boasting the highest concentration of living Grail Knights in the entire Old World. Bohemond himself, wielding his ancient dragon-bone mace, leads his heavy lances on ceaseless monster hunts, ensuring Bastonne remains the eternal beacon of chivalric honor and martial perfection.
bordeleaux: Bordeleaux dominates the southwest coast of Bretonnia, famous across civilization as the undisputed wine capital of the Old World. Its sun-drenched rolling hills are blanketed with endless vineyards producing exquisite vintages shipped to Altdorf, Marienburg, and Tilea. The sprawling coastal capital of Bordeleaux is divided between the inland nobility devout to the Lady and sea-hardened sailors who worship Manann, God of the Sea. Governed by the austere, duty-bound Duke Alberic de Bordeleaux, the dukedom maintains one of the largest battle fleets in the kingdom. Alberic's knights, known as the Knights of the Trident, undergo rigorous maritime training, adept at fighting aboard warships and leading thunderous cavalry assaults across coastal salt marshes to repel pirate reavers and sea monsters.
carcassonne: Carcassonne guards the far southern border of Bretonnia, flanked by the arid passes of Estalia and the enigmatic borders of Athel Loren. Since the founding of the kingdom, Carcassonne has borne the heaviest military burden of all: holding the southern frontier against endless invasions of Orcs and Goblins pouring out of the Badlands and mountains. Ruled by Duke Huebald, Carcassonne is a land of craggy limestone hills and fortified hill villages. Uniquely in Bretonnia, even peasant shepherds carry deadly shepherd's crooks and recurve bows, trained to battle greenskins from childhood. Carcassonne's knights, battle-scarred and pragmatic, fight alongside pastoral levies, viewing their perpetual warfare as a noble shield that preserves the arts, poetry, and serenity of the inner dukedoms.
aquitaine: Aquitaine is the most fertile, sunlit, and idyllic dukedom in Bretonnia, yet paradoxically the most violent internally. Blessed with rich loam farmlands and gentle hills sloping toward the western sea, Aquitaine produces abundant grain and livestock. However, its noble houses are notorious for their fierce pride, stubborn independence, and centuries-old blood feuds, settling boundary disputes and minor insults through lethal judicial jousts. Governed by the pious Duke Armand d'Aquitaine—the royal battle standard-bearer—the dukedom also bears the dark scars of the Red Duke, an ancient Blood Dragon vampire who once terrorized the land. Aquitaine's knights are among the most lethal duelists in the world, striving to turn their brawling energy outward to defend their sunny homeland from evil.
brionne: Brionne is the cultural and romantic jewel of southern Bretonnia, nestled along the sparkling azure waters of the Southern Sea. Bordered by Aquitaine, Quenelles, and Carcassonne, Brionne is celebrated as the birthplace of the troubadours, courtly love, and chivalric romance. The capital city of Brionne is an architectural masterpiece of soaring spires, marble colonnades, and rose gardens overlooking the bay. Governed by Duke Theodoric, Brionne's court prizes poetry, song, and beautiful tapestries as highly as the martial arts. Yet its knights are far from decadent fops: when war calls, Brionne's noble cavaliers charge into the fray with poetic fervor and manic courage, riding into battle in pursuit of eternal songs and glorious legends worthy of the Lady's divine grace.
quenelles: Quenelles is the largest dukedom in Bretonnia by territorial expanse, dominating the southeastern plains bordering the primeval enchanted forest of Athel Loren. Having annexed the ruined lands of Cuileux after that dukedom was annihilated by greenskins in ancient times, Quenelles carries a deep, ancestral hatred of Orcs and Goblins. Governed by the pious and grief-stricken Duke Tancred II, Quenelles must guard against savage greenskin tribes entrenched in the jagged volcanic crags of Massif Orcal, while maintaining uneasy border peace with the enigmatic Wood Elves. Quenelles's knights are seasoned frontier veterans who have fought alongside Treemen and Grail Knights alike, patrolling the borders day and night to ensure greenskin savagery never breaches the heartlands of Bretonnia.
mousillon: Mousillon is the open wound, eternal shame, and dark nightmare of Bretonnia—a cursed, derelict dukedom smothered in foul, bubbling swamps and choking toxic mists along the River Grismerie. Once the proudest dukedom in the realm, Mousillon fell into disgrace during the Red Pox and the treacherous Affair of the False Grail, after which its ducal title was revoked and its lands quarantined. Today, crooked castle ruins sink slowly into black mud, surrounded by plague-ridden marshes where the dead refuse to rest. Led by Mallobaude the Serpent—the renegade bastard son of King Louen who rejected the Lady after drinking of the Grail—Mousillon has become a gathering ground for black knights, necromancers, and vampires. They plot to tear down the hypocritical chivalry of Couronne and drown Bretonnia in an unholy tide of iron and sorcery.
karak_kadrin: Karak Kadrin—famed among mankind as Slayer Keep—is the most legendary dwarf citadel in the World's Edge Mountains after the Everpeak itself. It straddles the eastern terminus of Peak Pass, the ancient caravan road cutting through the mountains between the dark steppes and the northern Empire. Ruled by King Ungrim Ironfist, the Slayer King, Karak Kadrin bears a unique and tragic burden: its royal lineage is bound by the sacred Slayer Oath to seek death in combat against terrible beasts, yet simultaneously bound by the King's Oath to protect and govern the hold. Consequently, Karak Kadrin serves as the global spiritual sanctuary of the Cult of Grimnir. Crested, orange-haired Slayers flock here from every hold to offer prayers at the Great Shrine of Grimnir before marching into Peak Pass to slay trolls, dragons, and giants. Supported by heavy artillery batteries and resolute ironbreaker phalanxes, Karak Kadrin stands as an unbreakable redoubt barring the eastern horrors from the west.
karak_angazhar: Karak Angazhar is nestled in the craggy valleys of the Black Mountains, acting as a crucial transit bastion between the southern Empire and the Border Princes. While the Black Mountains lack the immense gromril deposits and ancient rune halls of the World's Edge Mountains, Angazhar has flourished through terraced alpine agriculture, highland cattle ranching, and master tool-forging. Ruled by King Bragarik, the hold is famed for its wide network of Mountain Rangers—hardy scouts who patrol high passes in snowshoes, armed with heavy crossbows and throwing axes. Maintaining protective protectorates over neighboring human settlements, Angazhar ensures that the mountain passes connecting Reikland to the southern frontiers remain free of night goblins and mountain trolls.
karak_azgaraz: Karak Azgaraz—meaning 'Hold of the Fearless Axes'—perches high upon the eastern slopes of Eagle Peak in the Grey Mountains, roughly sixty miles south of the Imperial city of Ubersreik. Older than the Empire itself, the hold was originally established as a humble trading post before the War of the Beard, expanding into a magnificent subterranean redoubt as refugees from lost eastern holds migrated westward. Governed by King Thuringar Beastbreaker, Karak Azgaraz controls extensive copper, iron, and tin mines beneath the crags. Its smiths and stonemasons maintain close commercial ties with the Imperial burghers of Ubersreik, trading mastercrafted tools and weapons for timber and grain while holding the mountain crests against marauding orcs and mountain chimerae.
karak_eksfilaz: Karak Eksfilaz—the 'Hold of the Aspen Winds'—sits atop the highest crags of the Vaults, the shattered highland knot separating Wissenland from Tilea. Perched at dizzying altitudes, it is renowned throughout the Old World for its exquisite white and grey marble quarries, which have supplied stone for temples, palaces, and statues from Altdorf to Miragliano. Under King Skarf Redbeard, Eksfilaz has transformed into an opulent commercial emporium where dwarfen merchants trade refined marble, silver filigree, and forged breastplates for southern wine, olive oil, and grain. Its precipitous cliffs and narrow suspension bridges make it virtually unassailable to greenskins, guarding the highland passes between human empires.
karak_gantuk: Karak Gantuk is one of the most modest yet stubbornly resilient dwarfen holds in the Black Mountains, tucked into the secluded peaks between the Empire and the Border Princes. Housing a tight-knit population of roughly two thousand five hundred adult dwarfs, Gantuk has long lived in the shadow of its mighty neighbor Karak Hirn. Yet under King Skagg Hammerfist, Gantuk's miners and tunnel fighters take fierce pride in their quiet self-sufficiency. Its underground chambers feature ingeniously counterweighted iron portcullises that can seal galleries in seconds, allowing its compact garrison of Ironbreakers to hold off vastly superior numbers of night goblins and cave beasts.
karak_hirn: Karak Hirn—the 'Horn Hold'—is the largest, wealthiest, and most powerful dwarfen realm in the Black Mountains. Its defining marvel is not merely its rich gold and iron lodes, but the natural acoustics of Mount Hirn. A colossal natural cavern near the summit acts as a gigantic wind horn, channeling mountain gales through carved stone chambers to produce a thunderous, low-frequency bellow heard across fifteen miles. Ruled by King Alrik Ranulfsson—a staunch traditionalist who rides into battle standing upon the ancient Shield of Gorrim—Karak Hirn leads the confederation of Black Mountain holds. Its semaphore towers and acoustic horn allow it to summon clan throngs within hours, crushing greenskin warbands beneath an iron wall of Gromril armor and runic stone throwers.
karak_izor: Karak Izor—known to humanity as 'Copper Mountain'—is the largest, oldest, and most formidable dwarfen realm outside the World's Edge Mountains, anchoring the rugged core of the Vaults. Guarded by glacial chasms, sheer granite walls, and treacherous scree slopes, nature itself provides Izor with an impenetrable rampart. Governed by King Kazran Grimbrow, the hold rests atop the richest deposits of copper, tin, and zinc in the known world, making it the premier bronze and brass foundry of Karaz Ankor. Its deep halls roar with steam-powered stamps and smelting furnaces, producing heavy armor, cannons, and gyrocopter components that supply dwarfen holds from the Grey Mountains to the southern shores.
karak_kaferkammaz: Karak Kaferkammaz—meaning 'Hold of the Marble Strata'—sits upon the highest wind-scoured pinnacle of the Vaults. Like its sister hold Eksfilaz, its wealth is anchored in the quarrying of flawless colored marble, prized by architects across the Old World. Under King Durak Granitebrow, Kaferkammaz serves as the grand communication hub of the southern mountain ranges. Its precipitous exterior bastions house advanced Gyrocopter landing pads and semaphore mirrors that relay intelligence between Karak Izor and the northern human kingdoms. In times of war, its mountain scouts and gyrocopters spot enemy movements weeks before they reach the valleys, directing dwarfen vengeance with surgical precision.
karak_norn: Karak Norn—the 'Barren Earth Hold'—is the premier dwarfen citadel in the Grey Mountains, perched atop a massive highland plateau directly overlooking the magical borders of Athel Loren and the lowlands of Bretonnia. Founded by waves of refugees fleeing the fall of Mount Silverspear centuries ago, its people cherish the ancestral relics and runic knowledge saved from the east. Governed by King Brokk Ironpick, Karak Norn controls valuable iron and silver mines, as well as secret deposits of rare gemstones. While maintaining a tense, watchful truce with the Wood Elves below, its warriors are seasoned underground fighters who patrol the Grey Mountain crests to safeguard dwarfen sovereignty.
karak_zhufbar: Karak Zhufbar—the 'Torrent Gate'—is a titanic subterranean industrial complex carved into the sheer canyon walls of the World's Edge Mountains, overlooking the vast, dark expanse of Lake Black Water. Unlike other holds famed for gold or gems, Zhufbar is celebrated as the industrial and technological heart of Karaz Ankor. The thunderous waterfalls draining the lake are channeled through tens of thousands of waterwheels, triphammers, and hydraulic pistons that power the greatest concentration of foundries in the dwarfen world. Ruled by King Morgrim Ironforge, Zhufbar is the primary center of the Dwarf Engineers Guild, working day and night casting cannons, assembling gyrocopters, and forging gromril armor that sustains dwarfen armies throughout the Old World.
karak_ziflin: Karak Ziflin is a rugged dwarfen citadel clinging to the steep northern slopes of the Grey Mountains, positioned just north of the Axe Bite Pass. Though compact in size, housing approximately two thousand adult dwarfs, Ziflin occupies an invaluable strategic location commanding the western mountain approaches connecting Bretonnia with the Empire. Governed by King Rorek Granitehand, Ziflin derives its prosperity from guarding mercantile pack trains, collecting mountain tolls, and mining iron and lead. Its tunnel fighters and crossbowmen coordinate closely with the garrisons of Montfort to keep the Axe Bite Pass clear of mountain orcs and ambushers, acting as a crucial western link in Karaz Ankor's defenses.
bad_axes: The Bad Axes Tribe is entrenched in the sheer, razor-sharp gorges of the northern Grey Mountains overlooking Marienburg and the eastern marches of Couronne. The tribe derives its fearsome moniker from a religious obsession with colossal iron choppas—every Bad Axe boy is taught from spawning that an axe has failed its duty unless buried deep in shattered bone. The tribe's defining terror is their mastery over Hagranim beasts—feral, semi-reptilian highland predators whose clawed pads can scale vertical cliffs. Mounted upon these beasts, Bad Axe raiders bypass fortified mountain chokepoints, descending from sheer precipices onto the supply lines and baggage trains of Bretonnian knightly patrols. Led by their brutal Warboss Bonechewer Ironjaw, the tribe continually raids the fertile pastures of Couronne, amassing scrap iron and stoking their bellicose frenzy for an apocalyptic descent upon the lowlands.
black_sunz: The Black Sunz are an elite, purebred Black Orc tribe whose lineage traces directly back to the dark breeding experiments of the Chaos Dwarfs in Zharr-Naggrund. Darker-skinned, immensely heavily muscled, and devoid of the comedic buffoonery of common greenskins, the Black Sunz operate with chilling, militaristic efficiency. Under Warboss Gorlak Blacksun, they march in regimented ranks, clad in thick blackened iron plates and wielding massive two-handed greataxes. Driven by burning racial hatred against their former slavers and contempt for unruly common orcs, the Black Sunz conquer lesser mobs through brutal discipline rather than noisy Waaagh! frenzy. They seek out the toughest enemy battle lines—dwarf ironbreakers and imperial greatswords—to prove that the Black Sunz are the undisputed apex predators of the Old World.
crooked_eye: The Crooked Eye Tribe possesses a storied history of catastrophic fall from grace. Once among the most terrifying orc powers in the Badlands, they rampaged across the World's Edge Mountains under Warboss Ruglud Bonechewer, devastating dwarf outposts and Imperial border garrisons. However, an ill-fated eastern expedition into the Dark Lands saw them crushed by Chaos Dwarf blunderbuss lines, reducing the proud horde to scattered, vengeful bands. Today, under One-Eye Crooked-Tooth, the survivors have re-emerged with a pragmatic twist: they eagerly scavenge heavy armor, crossbows, and dwarf artillery, forming the infamous Ruglud's Armoured Orcs mercenary tradition. Driven by brooding spite, they seek to reforge their horde and take bloody retribution upon any who dare mock their fallen glory.
deff_grindaz: The Deff Grindaz (Death Grindaz) are an embattled, ferociously aggressive orc tribe entrenched in the jagged volcanic crags of Massif Orcal and the southern Grey Mountains. Trapped like meat between two grinding millstones, the tribe faces ceaseless hostile pressure from three converging fronts: Bretonnian knightly crusades to the west, Imperial frontier patrols to the north, and wood elf border ambushes to the south. This constant peril has turned the Deff Grindaz into manic, cornered beasts. Led by Spinebreaker Ironfist, their warriors wield jagged iron maces and serrated cleavers, throwing themselves into battle with suicidal desperation. Knowing that defeat means total eradication, they fight with terrifying fury, seeking to blast open an escape corridor into the fertile Bretonnian plains.
iron_tribe: The Iron Tribe represents the battle-scarred veteran remnants of the greatest greenskin invasion in elven history: Grom the Paunch's legendary Waaagh! that successfully invaded the magical island of Ulthuan. Though Grom's war chariot was ultimately brought down beneath the towers of Yvresse, surviving orc veterans returned across the Great Ocean carrying stolen elven artifacts, enchanted gems, and the ironclad conviction that greenskins can conquer anything. Governed by Warboss Ironjaw Steelbelly, the Iron Tribe fights with an atypical degree of cohesion, their heavy choppas reinforced with salvaged elven ithilmar and dwarfen iron. Living upon the glory of their past oceanic crusade, they are determined to amass enough boyz to launch another continent-shattering invasion.
massif_choppas: The Massif Choppas are Bretonnia's most persistent internal ulcer—an ancient orc tribe entrenched within the volcanic caverns of Massif Orcal that has defied eradication for three thousand years. Their defining obsession is the colossal, two-handed great choppa—a brutal slab of jagged iron twice the height of a man that requires immense muscle to swing. Led by Big Choppa Skullcleaver, their warriors leap from volcanic fissures to cleave mounted knights and heavy horses in twain with single overhead blows. Having survived dozens of royal Errantry Wars by retreating into toxic subterranean lava tubes, the Massif Choppas continually re-emerge to raid the rich vineyards of Quenelles and Bastonne, laughing in the face of chivalric honor.
neck_snappers: The Necksnappers (Nexsnappaz) are widely feared as the most formidable and disciplined Black Orc tribe in the Old World, commanded by the notorious Warboss Morglum Necksnapper. Unlike common greenskin mobs that degenerate into brawling chaos, the Necksnappers advance in silence, marching in lockstep behind towering totems. Their name comes from their terrifying trademark execution: grabbing armored foes by the helmet and snapping their cervical spines with a single twist of gauntleted hands. Morglum famously proclaimed: 'Let 'em talk, we'll do da smashin'!' Operating with professional military ruthlessness, the Necksnappers crush enemy battle lines through sheer, concentrated kinetic violence, aiming to smash the proudest castles of humanity and dwarfs into rubble.
skull_smasherz: The Skull Smasherz are recognized as the supreme greenskin power in the Grey Mountains, holding a stranglehold over Axe Bite Pass—the primary overland conduit connecting Reikland in the Empire with Montfort in Bretonnia. Governed by Warboss Uglok Cleavetooth, the Skull Smasherz are remarkably cunning raiders who understand the value of toll extortion and supply choke points. Rather than burning caravans, they ambush them from high canyon ledges, looting gold, draft horses, and weapons while taking heavy tribute. Entrenched in hidden cave fortresses along the pass, they continually fend off both Imperial State Troops and Bretonnian knights, turning the most vital trade highway in the west into a deadly gauntlet of iron and bone.
bloody_spearz: The Bloody Spearz are one of the most infamous Night Goblin tribes in the World's Edge Mountains, infesting the labyrinth of abandoned dwarf mines along the vital Silver Road. Their name comes from their signature tactic: striking silently from pitch-black ventilation shafts and side tunnels with long spears dripping with lethal cave-spider venom. Under Warboss Gnashrak, they operate as subterranean highwaymen, ambushing dwarfen iron convoys and Imperial merchant trains in the dark. Accompanied by swarms of snarling Cave Squigs and Fanatics whirling massive spiked iron balls on chains, the Bloody Spearz amass hoards of gold and gromril, terrorizing the subterranean arteries of the Old World.
red_eye: The Red Eye Tribe represents the largest and most terrifying Night Goblin confederation in the Old World, occupying the colossal fallen dwarf citadel of Karak Ungor—now known throughout greenskin lore as Red Eye Mountain. Once the deepest and richest mining citadel of the Dwarf Empire, its subterranean galleries plunge miles into the earth. Today, its grand rune halls are infested by hundreds of thousands of Night Goblins led by the cunning Warboss Scareye Blackhat. Cultivating toxic mad cap mushrooms and breeding monstrous colossal squigs in the subterranean dark, the Red Eyes wage a constant three-way war against encroaching Skaven from below and vengeful dwarfen reclamation throngs from above, holding the mountain as an impenetrable subterranean fortress.
black_pit: The Black Pit Tribe—feared across the Empire as the dread Spider Cult—is a terrifying society of Forest Goblins dwelling in the fetid, shadow-choked depths of the Drakwald Forest. Centered around the Black Pit, a bottomless chasmic rift in the earth, they worship the Great Spider God with fanatical devotion. Unlike mountain goblins, these forest stalkers ride giant poisonous spiders that scuttle silently across the canopy, dropping onto unwary Imperial patrols in showers of venomous fangs. Under the fanatical Manylegs the Web Prophet, their greatest terrors are the colossal Arachnarok Spiders—titanic, house-sized arachnids mounted with crude wooden howdahs packed with archers. Weaving suffocating webs across whole forest sectors, they sacrifice captured villagers to their eight-legged gods in gruesome midnight rituals.
reavaz: The Reavaz are a nomadic tribe of common goblins who survive on the harsh fringes of the Old World through sheer cowardice, low cunning, and shameless opportunism. Lacking the colossal size of orcs or the deep fortresses of night goblins, the Reavaz are master hit-and-run scavengers. Led by Broken Fang Grib, the tribe relies on packs of snarling giant wolves to outrun retribution. Mounted upon wolfback, Reavaz raiders circle isolated peasant cottages, lone merchant wagons, and straggling baggage trains, shooting clouds of crude arrows before vanishing into the mists at the first sight of armored knights or dwarf warriors. By never fighting fair and always running away, the Reavaz endure while prouder tribes perish in battle.
sylvania: Sylvania is the most infamous cursed realm in the Old World—a bleak, haunted province permanently blanketed beneath leaden grey storm clouds on the Empire's eastern frontier, wedged between Stirland, Ostermark, and the World's Edge Mountains. Castle Drakenhof serves as the nocturnal seat of the von Carstein dynasty—a colossal basalt citadel rising from a jagged black ridge like a jagged tooth. Governed by the cunning and supremely ambitious Count Mannfred von Carstein, Sylvania is an open cemetery where mortal peasants live lives of quiet terror, locking their doors before sunset and hanging garlic and Morr's charms above their lintels. Through mastery of the dark wind Dhar and the forbidden necromancy of Nagash, the von Carsteins command endless hosts of skeletons, wights, grave guard, and vargheists. Sylvania's rulers do not view themselves as mere monsters, but as the rightful, immortal heirs to the Imperial throne of mankind.
blooddragons: The Blood Dragons represent the martial pinnacle of the five great vampire bloodlines, founded by the tragic and peerless knight Abhorash. Their ancestral sanctuary—Blood Keep—perches high upon a sheer precipice in the Grey Mountains, guarding the mountain route between the Empire and Bretonnia. Once a noble human knightly order dedicated to Saint Origo, the citadel fell into darkness when Walach Harkon arrived, slaying the garrison in single combat and turning the bravest knights into immortal Blood Knights. Rejecting cowardice, necromantic hordes, and decadent politics, the Blood Dragons seek only martial perfection and martial glory. Mounted upon nightmare barded steeds and clad in crimson plate, they wander the earth seeking worthy champions, dragons, and terrible beasts to duel, hoping to follow Abhorash in overcoming the curse of the Red Thirst.
necrarchs: The Necrarchs are an esoteric, scholarly order of vampires founded by Wsoran, high priest of Nagash, who place the pursuit of forbidden dark knowledge above all mortal concerns. Possessing neither unified kingdoms, glittering courts, nor standing armies, Necrarch masters dwell as solitary hermits within crumbling towers, subterranean crypts, and desolate barrow mounds across the Old World. Centuries of deep communion with Dhar and warpstone dust have warped their immortal bodies into grotesque, gaunt, bat-like horrors with withered flesh, needle teeth, and sunken, glowing eyes. Despising the living and finding feeding distasteful, they dream of a peaceful, silent world where all life is extinguished and only the obedient dead remain, spending centuries calculating cosmic equations and deciphering the primordial hieroglyphs of ancient Nehekhara.
brasskeep: Brass Keep is the most sinister, festering scar within the very heart of the Empire—an ancient, cyclopean fortress built into the caldera of a colossal meteor crater atop the Middle Mountains between Hochland and Middenland. Pre-dating the coming of Sigmar, the keep was once an Imperial stronghold before falling to a nightmarish pestilential siege. Today, it stands as a defiled citadel dedicated to Nurgle, the Plague Lord. Green, noxious miasmas spill from its brass-bound parapets, while rusted gates open to reveal hordes of bloated Plaguebearers, swarms of Nurglings, and putrid Rot Knights. Operating deep behind Imperial lines, the pestilent abominations of Brass Keep cultivate unholy plagues, poisoning mountain aquifers and spreading horrific epidemics through the northern provinces in praise of their benevolent dark god.
athel_loren: Athel Loren is not a realm of castles, walls, and paved roads, but an ancient, sentient, and semi-divine woodland sprawling between southern Bretonnia and the Grey Mountains. As the oldest enchanted forest in the Old World, its tangled groves channel the densest concentrations of nature magic outside Ulthuan. Governed by the immortal King in the Woods, Orion, and the Fay Queen Ariel, the forest is divided into twelve distinct realms protected by the Asrai—the Wood Elves. Deepwood Scouts, Waywatchers, and wrathful ancient Treemen guard the hidden glades with lethal marksmanship and root-strangling magic. Athel Loren does not recognize the laws of mortal men: any human woodsman, orc raiding party, or beastman herd that breaches its enchanted borders becomes quarry in the merciless Wild Hunt, slain without warning to feed the sacred earth.
laurelorn: Laurelorn Forest—celebrated among mankind as the Golden Wood—is the most unique elven kingdom in the Old World. Spanning the ancient woodland between Nordland, Middenland, and the Wasteland, Laurelorn is not a realm of the Asrai, but the sovereign domain of the Eonir—the 'People of Memory'. Tracing their lineage back to the original High Elven colonists who refused to abandon the continent following the War of the Beard, the Eonir maintain a sophisticated balance of courtly High Elven diplomacy and wilderness woodland archery. Ruled from the hidden treetop court of Tor Linn by Queen Marrisith, Laurelorn fiercely defends its independence against human lumberjacks from Nordland while maintaining cautious diplomatic treaties with the Emperor, standing as an ancient elven redoubt on the northern rim of civilization.
